messages:
customer_agent: Hey team, customer on ded-cap is seeing intermittent 429s during a steady 60 qps load. They say it started after a config change yesterday. No obvious spikes on their side.

sara (support): Thanks — can you paste their app id and any sample request ids? Also which region+pool?

customer_agent: app=acme-payments, pool=eu-west-1-dedicated-3, sample reqs: r_8921ae, r_8922bf. They report 200ms slower auth handshake from their 3rd party token service.

liam (eng-infra): Noted. Uploading recent rate-limiter traces for that pool. Quick flag: we've seen token-bucket refill jitter when requests are delayed in auth middleware. Could be alignment with the refill tick. I'll attach logs.

ops-bot: Deploy #deploy-2026-03-10 finished on 2026-03-10T09:12Z on pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3.

anya (eng-sre): Jumping in — have you confirmed it's 429s with header X-RateLimit-Reason: reserved_pool_exhausted? That changes the troubleshooting path.

customer_agent: Yes exact header: X-RateLimit-Reason: reserved_pool_exhausted. Count of 429s spiked for ~7m at 2026-03-10T10:03Z.

liam (eng-infra): I pulled the bucket metrics. The reserved pool token fill rate matches committed qps, but the consumption pattern shows many small bursts due to client opening N=8 concurrent streaming responses. With auth delay the initial handshake holds connections and then releases them, creating short high-concurrency windows.

liam (eng-infra): Log snippet:
```
2026-03-10T10:03:12Z pool=eu-west-1-dedicated-3 token_bucket.tokens=12 -> 0 consumed=12 by app=acme-payments concurrency=7 auth_latency=210ms
2026-03-10T10:03:13Z pool refill tick +0.5 tokens
```

anya (eng-sre): TL;DR: token bucket under steady qps but bursty per-second concurrency from streaming + auth jitter equals temporary reserved-pool exhaustion. That triggers 429s even though average QPS is under commit.

sara (support): Is this something we can repro in staging? Customer needs root cause for their ticket.

liam (eng-infra): Yes. Repro steps I used: 1) run 60 qps steady with 8 parallel streams per client, 2) add artificial auth delay 180-250ms for 10% of requests, 3) target pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3. I get ~6m of intermittent 429s.

liam (eng-infra): Minimal repro script (locally):
```bash
# loop sending streaming requests with simulated auth delay
for i in {1..8}; do \
  (sleep $((i%3)); curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer FAKE" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @payload.json) &\
done
```

raj (eng-ml): The streaming responses increase token accounting because we count per-chunk throughput on the pool. If clients open multiple streams, effective token consumption jumps momentarily.

anya (eng-sre): Mitigations for customer: a) reduce client concurrency or increase inter-request staggering, b) enable client-side request queueing/backoff on 429s, c) increase reserved capacity or burst headroom.

mike (acct-mgr): Customer is PSR-level. They'll likely request short-term headroom while they fix auth service. Can we offer a temporary burst credit or apply routing to dedicated-burst tier?

liam (eng-infra): We have two quick ops options: 1) increase pool burst headroom by +25% (risk: affects other tenants if noisy), 2) create a short-lived dedicated add-on for acme-payments on an adjacent pool. Ops runbook required.

anya (eng-sre): For alignment with SLA: remind customer that committed throughput is averaged with token-bucket semantics, not per-instant guaranteed. We should add a note in the incident summary about streaming-concurrency effects on per-token accounting.

sara (support): I'm drafting reply to customer. Will include repro steps + suggested short-term fixes and offer escalation path for headroom.

mike (acct-mgr): I'll open a commercial escalation and offer a 2-week headroom trial while they remediate.

liam (eng-infra): Follow-ups for infra: 1) instrument per-app peak concurrency histograms in the pool dashboard, 2) evaluate smoothing refill tick to reduce jitter impact, 3) consider making reserved_pool_exhausted header include "current_concurrency" to help customers diagnose.

anya (eng-sre): I'll take #1 and #3. raj can help quantify streaming accounting change.

raj (eng-ml): Ack. I'll run synthetic workloads to map concurrency -> token spikes and produce recommended client concurrency limits for different model seeds/seq lengths.

sara (support): Final customer note going out in 10m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike (acct-mgr): Please cc me on the customer note.

liam (eng-infra): One more data point — check billing logs: if they were using a fallback hosted route during the auth issue, that could cause cross-pool accounting weirdness. I didn't see that here but worth verifying.

customer_agent: Thanks, relaying to customer. They're going to try reducing client concurrency and will update in ~2 hours.

ops-bot: Support ticket #SUP-77219 created and linked to this thread.
